classification.difficultyReason: Rewrite reciprocal and quotient ratios, preserve domain restrictions, then factor a quadratic in sine without losing zero solutions.

answer.short:
$\theta=0^\circ,\ 180^\circ,\ 360^\circ$.

Rewrite in sine and cosine, then factor; retain the zero-sine solutions.
answer.worked:
The original equation requires $\cos\theta\ne0$, so $\theta\ne90^\circ,270^\circ$.

Using $\sec\theta=\frac{1}{\cos\theta}$ and $\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$:

$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta}&=\frac{2\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\\\sin^2\theta&=2\sin\theta\\\sin^2\theta-2\sin\theta&=0\\\sin\theta(\sin\theta-2)&=0\end{align*}$$

Thus $\sin\theta=0$ or $\sin\theta=2$. Since $-1\le\sin\theta\le1$, the second case has no solutions.

For $0^\circ\le\theta\le360^\circ$, $\sin\theta=0$ gives $\theta=0^\circ,180^\circ,360^\circ$. Each has nonzero cosine and makes both sides of the original equation zero.
